chunks: Aban, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
Supplication is made for the deceased when he is placed in his grave, and the grave is raised above the ground by four fingers.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended measurement for raising a grave above ground level in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific timing of the supplication for the deceased, occurring precisely as the grave is being covered and the earth is raised. It establishes the physical standard for grave elevation at four fingers' width, a measurement widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence to distinguish the grave from the surrounding ground while maintaining modesty. This practice underscores the continuity of communal care and prayer for the departed during the immediate transition from burial to the afterlife.

en.hubeali:
Aban, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Supplicate for the deceased when he enters his pit (grave), and raise the grave above the ground by four fingers’.
en.sarwar: 10. Aban has narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Prayers are said when a deceased is placed in his grave and the surface of the grave is raised above the ground by four fingers.’”
